UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                            BEFORE THE
              FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION



Southwest Power Pool, Inc.                   )      Docket No.      ER26-247-000
                                             )



             MOTION FOR LEAVE TO ANSWER AND ANSWER OF
                    SOUTHWEST POWER POOL, INC.

       Pursuant to Rules 212 and 213 of the Rules of Practice and Procedure of the Federal

Energy Regulatory Commission (the “Commission” or “FERC”), 18 C.F.R. §§ 385.212

and 385.213, Southwest Power Pool, Inc. (“SPP”) submits this Motion for Leave to Answer

and Answer1 in response to the comments filed in this proceeding.




1
       SPP respectfully requests leave to respond to the comments filed in this proceeding
       to aid the Commission’s decision-making process. The Commission regularly
       permits answers for good cause shown, and the Commission has held that answers
       are permitted when they ensure a more accurate and complete record, clarify the
       issues, or provide useful and relevant information that will assist the Commission
       in its deliberative process. See, e.g., City Utils. of Springfield, Mo. v. Sw. Power
       Pool, Inc., 168 FERC ¶ 61,085, at P 51 (2019) (“We accept the answers . . . because
       they have provided information that assisted us in our decision-making process.”),
       order on reh’g & clarification, 170 FERC ¶ 61,024 (2020); Sw. Power Pool, Inc.,
       144 FERC ¶ 61,059, at P 17 (2013) (same) order on reh’g & compliance, 149
       FERC ¶ 61,048 (2014), order on reh’g & compliance filing, 151 FERC ¶ 61,045
       (2015), petition for review dismissed sub nom. LSP Transmission Holdings, LLC v.
       FERC, 700 F. App’x 1 (D.C. Cir. 2017) (per curiam); Morgan Stanley Capital Grp.,
       Inc. v. N.Y. Indep. Sys. Operator, Inc., 93 FERC ¶ 61,017, at 61,036 (2000)
       (accepting an answer as “helpful in the development of the record”). SPP’s silence
       on statements contained in comments or protests should not be considered
       agreement or acquiescence to any unaddressed conclusions or statements.
 I.     BACKGROUND

       On October 24, 2025, SPP submitted revisions to its Open Access Transmission

Tariff2 to add new Attachments BA and BB, which contain a proposed High Impact Large

Load process and a High Impact Large Load Generation Assessment process, respectively.3

       Several parties filed motions to intervene.4

       On November 4, 2025, Eolian L.P. filed a motion requesting an extension of time

to November 24, 2025, to submit comments in this proceeding. On November 7, 2025, the

SPP Transmission Owner Group filed an answer in response to the motion for extension

II.    ANSWER

       Apart from the Enchanted Rock Comments, all commentors support the

Commission approving SPP’s High Impact Large Load Filing as just and reasonable and

not unduly discriminatory or preferential. Although the Enchanted Rock Comments

request specific modifications to SPP’s High Impact Large Load Filing, the Enchanted

 Rock Comments do not argue or allege that SPP’s proposal, unmodified, is unjust or

unreasonable.

       Under Federal Power Act (“FPA”) section 205,12 SPP must show only that its Tariff

filing is just and reasonable, not that it is the best approach, better than others’ preferred

alternatives, nor even better than the current Tariff approach. 13 In the FPA section 205

context, the Commission’s role is “essentially passive and reactive” and therefore is limited

to “evaluating the confined proposal.”14

       As noted in the filed comments, there is overwhelming support for SPP’s High

Impact Large Load Filing. More importantly, no commentor offered any claims that the

Commission should reject SPP’s filing as unjust or unreasonable. SPP’s High Impact Large

Load Filing, based on SPP’s initial filing and the supporting comments, is clearly a just

and reasonable proposal, and therefore, the Commission should approve.

13

       reasonable one.”); OXY USA, Inc. v. FERC, 64 F.3d 679, 692 (D.C. Cir. 1995)

       are reasonable—and does not extend to determining whether a proposed rate

       revisions need not be the best or the only reasonable methodology.” (internal

        A.      The Commission Should Accept SPP’s High Impact Large Load Filing
               Notwithstanding Enchanted Rock’s Proposed Modifications.

       Enchanted Rock generally supports SPP’s High Impact Large Load Filing but

suggests a modification to the proposal.15 As pointed out in the Enchanted Rock

Comments, SPP’s High Impact Large Load Filing provides that High Impact Large Load

Generator Assessment (“HILLGA”) requests cannot exceed the associated High Impact

Large Load’s (“HILL’s”) requested load, multiplied by the greater of: 1) 110% plus the

Planning Reserve Margin outlined in the HILLGA Study Agreement; or 2) 125%.16

Enchanted Rock proposes that this limit is not representative of actual on-site generation

capacity requirements given customer requirements for generation availability.17 To be

more representative of the actual on-site generation capacity needed, Enchanted Rock has

an alternative proposal to increase the 125% limitation to 150%.18

       Under FPA section 205, SPP is only required to show that its Tariff filing is just

and reasonable, not that it is the best approach, better than others’ preferred alternatives,

nor even better than the current Tariff approach.19 The Commission is limited in its review

to only that which was proposed in SPP’s High Impact Large Load Filing. Enchanted Rock

does not state that SPP’s filing is unjust and unreasonable, only that they prefer their

proposed alternative.

        SPP limited the size of the HILLGA requests in its proposal to ensure that the

Resource being studied would only have injection rights (i.e. Load Limited Resource

Interconnection Service) necessary to fully support the HILL. This limitation prevents the

generators from impacting other existing generator requests currently pending in an SPP

generator interconnection process

       SPP’s proposal uses existing capacity accreditation processes to limit the capacity

of the HILLGA Generating Facility request to the MW value necessary to support the

HILL. This means that the allowable nameplate capacity for the HILLGA Generating

Facility will vary depending on the technology and fuel type used. This will provide better

targeted limits so that the HILLGA Generating Facility is able to provide only the amount

of capacity needed to support the HILL.

       SPP proposes to use a two-step process to determine the allowable nameplate

capacity for a HILLGA Generating Facility to provide clear guidance on the size of the

facility. First, SPP will determine the allowable capacity amount necessary to support the

HILL by taking the MW value of the HILL and multiplying it by 110% plus the PRM or

by 125%, whichever is higher. Second, SPP will divide the allowable capacity amount by

the existing capacity accreditation value of the proposed HILLGA Generating Facility to

arrive at the allowable nameplate capacity number. Below are two examples that

demonstrate this two-step process for a 100 MW HILL:




                                            6
        Example 1:

              Technology and Fuel: Natural Gas Combustion Turbine with onsite fuel

              Supporting HILL: 100 MW

              Allowable Capacity Amount: 100 MW x 125%20 = 125MW

              Allowable Nameplate Capacity: 125 MW / 90.1% 21= 138.73 MW

       Example 2:

              Technology: Wind Farm

              Supporting HILL: 100 MW

              Allowable Capacity Amount: 100 MW x 125% = 125MW

              Allowable Nameplate Capacity: 125 MW / 19%22 = 657.89 MW


       SPP’s proposal to use accredited capacity plus a reasonable margin ensures that

SPP will only study a proposed HILLGA Generating Facility that is sized to meet the

capacity needs of the HILL. Nothing in the SPP Tariff prevents the HILLGA Generating

       B.      Proposed Reporting Requirement is not Needed

       SEIA requests “SPP to actively monitor and periodically report to the Commission

and to stakeholders on the effectiveness of the HILL and HILLGA frameworks to meet

rising demand and support the reliable integration of new, concentrated large loads and

local interconnection of associated generation resources.”23 SPP and its stakeholders

continuously monitor every service provided under its Tariff. Likewise, if the Commission

approves the HILL and HILLGA proposed Tariff revisions, SPP will monitor the

effectiveness of this HILL and HILLGA framework in addressing this exponential growth

in large loads. As such, an order requiring SPP to monitor the HILL and HILLGA

framework is unnecessary, and the Commission should deny SEIA’s suggestion for

reporting.

        C.     SPP Tariff Processes Remain Unchanged Other Than Those Proposed
              in SPP’s High Impact Large Load Filing.

       Eolian requests as follows:

              [I]n approving the HILLGA proposal, the Commission require SPP to
              clarify that the new pathway for HILLGA resources to serve particular
              HILLs does not remove or limit existing pathways for non HILLGA
              resources to serve particular HILLs. More particularly, FERC should
              require SPP to clarify that its tariff revisions do not restrict non HILLGA
              resources from specifically serving HILL load for purposes of
              demonstrating adequate designated or planned resources pursuant to the
              relevant transmission service study processes set forth in Attachments AQ
              and AX.24


        SPP’s High Impact Large Load Filing does not change the types of Resources that

are currently eligible to be studied in the processes outlined in Attachments AQ and AX of

the Tariff. Any Resource that is eligible to serve load through SPP transmission service

processes today will continue to be eligible if the Commission approves this filing, which

includes loads that qualify as HILLs. SPP’s High Impact Large Load Filing does not

contain any proposed Tariff language to the contrary. With this understanding, there is no

need for SPP to make any clarifications as requested by Eolian.




24

 III.     CONCLUSION

         SPP respectfully requests that the Commission accept this Answer to assist the

Commission in its decision-making process, find that SPP’s High Impact Large Load Filing

is just and reasonable, and issue an order accepting SPP’s High Impact Large Load Filing.
